newsitem.title: USA: Sen. McCain shows interest in presidential run.
newsitem.headline: Sen. McCain shows interest in presidential run.

text.p: By Alan Elsner, U.S. Political Correspondent
Republican Sen. John McCain thinks President Bill Clinton is the best politician he has ever seen.

The 60-year-old Arizona lawmaker, a Vietnam War hero and former prisoner or war, has good reason to study Clinton carefully. In an interview with Reuters, he said he has started to think about running for president himself.
The white-haired McCain is not willing to begin laying the groundwork for a presidential campaign right now, as some Republicans are already doing.
First, he wants to win re-election to his Senate seat in 1998. "However, if after I am re-elected the situation appears that I could be competitive, I would give consideration to that," he said.

"But there would have to be a climate where they (Republican voters) would want someone who is not a traditional conservative," added McCain, who has staked out an independent position, away from the party's mainstream, on issues such as campaign finance reform, normalisation of relations with Vietnam and protecting the environment.

That cautious statement of interest shows how far McCain's thinking has moved in recent weeks. In an interview with Congressional Quarterly in November, he offered a flat "no" when asked whether he would consider a presidential run.

Meanwhile, McCain is certain to be a leading Republican voice in the Senate on defence and foreign policy. This week he was elected chairman of the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee and he is spearheading a bipartisan effort to reform campaign finance laws to limit sharply the amount of money spent on election campaigns.

As chairman, McCain could win prominence on issues such as auto air bag safety, telecommunications product liability, and plans to rate television programmes for sex and violence. He will also have a voice on the controversial question of whether broadcast bands for digital television should be auctioned, which McCain strongly favours.

In the 1996 presidential election, McCain was a key adviser to Republican candidate Bob Dole. He spent many weeks accompanying Dole on the campaign trail and emerged with a new understanding of the demands of running for president.
He also acquired a grudging admiration for Clinton.
"I think President Clinton is the best politician I have ever seen. He has the best antennae and I have never seen anyone who could interact with an audience in the way he can," he said.

McCain got a mild rebuke from the Senate Ethics Committee in 1991 for his involvement in a savings and loan scandal, but that fall from grace is dwarfed by his war record. A Navy flier, he was shot down over Vietnam in 1967 and spent five years as a prisoner of war undergoing horrific tortures.
